brief:
Import restrictions on cigarettes are forcing Gaza's smoking population to ration supplies and endure withdrawal symptoms, We Are Not Numbers reported. Smokers describe difficult choices between purchasing cigarettes and meeting other basic needs as scarcity drives prices higher across the territory. The shortage has created a two-tier market where those with financial means secure supplies while others face prolonged deprivation.

The tobacco shortage adds another layer to the humanitarian pressures facing Gaza's residents already struggling with limited access to food, fuel, and medicine. Nicotine-dependent individuals report acute physical withdrawal symptoms alongside psychological strain as cigarette availability tightens under import restrictions. The crisis underscores how supply controls ripple through daily life in ways extending far beyond public health considerations.
dek: Restrictions on tobacco imports are forcing smokers to make hard choices and suffer from nicotine withdrawal.
title: Gaza tobacco ban pushes smokers into nicotine withdrawal crisis
